transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hey Doc. Um... well, I came in because I just feel like I got this motor running inside me all day long. It just don't ever shut off. Like, if I have to sit still at church, or out there in the clinic waiting room, or even just sitting around at home, I feel totally trapped. I just have to get up or do something. 

Which is why I was pacing out there by your magazines. You guys have a lot of old magazines, by the way. I saw a Sports Illustrated from like three years ago. The one with the baseball guy on the cover... I used to play baseball when I was a kid. Played shortstop, mostly 'cause you're always moving, you know? Coach said I had good hands but I couldn't ever stay in the dugout without messing with the bats or kicking the dirt. We went to the state championship that year, almost won the whole thing until Jimmy dropped a pop fly. 

But yeah... what was I saying? Right, if I gotta sit still, I just feel trapped. I gotta be moving.
When you feel that trapped, keyed-up feeling, is your mind also filled with worry most of the time?

Worry? Nah, not really. I mean, it ain't like I'm sitting there fretting about bills or the roof caving in or nothing. It's just... I just gotta move. My legs just want to go. It's like when you wind up one of them little toy cars and you hold the wheels, you know? You can feel it buzzing, just waiting to shoot across the floor. My nephew had one of them, a little red Corvette. We used to race 'em down the hallway at my sister's place. Man, she used to get so mad when we'd hit the baseboards and leave scuff marks. She's got this real nice hardwood floor, oak I think. Or maybe maple? I don't know, it's light colored. But yeah, she'd holler at us to take it outside, but it was raining that day, just pouring down buckets... so what are you gonna do, right? But no, I ain't worried about nothing in particular. Just can't stay put.
Have you felt this need to keep moving since you were a child?

Oh yeah, ever since I was a little kid. Back when I was a boy in school, it was real bad. The teachers, they were always moving my seat around 'cause I just could not stay put for the life of me. I'd be talking out of turn, just blurting stuff out, and I'd always get in big trouble for jumping up out of my chair before class was even done. I'd just be ready to go. 

Speaking of going, you know those old school bells? The big loud metal ones? My granddad had one of those mounted right on his front porch out in the country. He used to yank the rope and ring it when it was time for supper. He lived out on this big piece of land, had like fifty head of cattle... mostly Angus, I think. Black cows, anyway. I used to run around out there chasing the barn cats while everybody else was working. There was this one tomcat, missing half an ear, meanest thing you ever saw. Scratched me right down the arm once when I tried to pick him up near the tractor. Still got the scar... well, it's kind of faded now, but it bled a whole lot. 

What was I saying? Oh, right, yeah, school. So they'd stick my desk in the back, then move me to the front, then by the window... I liked the window, though. Could watch the cars go by on the highway. But yeah, it's been like this pretty much my whole life.
